title: Big bands, the cabaret tax and playing for dancing
summary: They discuss the lack of big bands in New Orleans, the cabaret tax ending dances, and George Lewis's band preferring to play for dancers.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

the eight yeah yeah it was after that you know really the the business on the wartime cabaret tax or whatever it was did pretty much we've talked about this of course and other people have too did pretty much wipe out uh dancing a lot of dance halls and a lot of dancing yeah and uh i think wiped out a lot of musicians yeah or bands at any rate that had worked for a long time i remember one of the things that we heard many times from musicians uh george lewis band in particular used they used to talk about how they had liked playing that they really liked it when they played for people to dance that they would and could and did play concerts but that the concerts weren't much fun that they got much more pleasure out of and much more stimulation out of playing for people to dance and i think that's probably true
